_help: Essential reading list shown on the page, in order. Edit, reorder or replace items freely; each needs a title, authors, year, venue, doi (or url) and a 'why' sentence.
intro: Read these in order if you are starting out in irrigation research with satellites and models. They move from why irrigation matters, to finding it, to measuring how much water is used and when.

items.title: Irrigation in the Earth system
items.authors: McDermid, S., Nocco, M., Lawston-Parker, P., et al.
items.why: Start here for the big picture: how irrigation changes temperature, rainfall and the carbon and nitrogen cycles, and which questions are still open.

items.title: A review of irrigation information retrievals from space and their utility for users
items.authors: Massari, C., Modanesi, S., Dari, J., et al.
items.why: A map of the field: the satellite data and methods used to map and quantify irrigation, set against what water managers actually need.

items.title: A global approach to estimate irrigated areas – a comparison between different data and statistics
items.authors: Meier, J., Zabel, F., Mauser, W.
items.why: Shows why irrigated-area maps disagree, by comparing a satellite-based global map with irrigation statistics.

items.title: Mapping three decades of annual irrigation across the US High Plains Aquifer using Landsat and Google Earth Engine
items.authors: Deines, J.M., Kendall, A.D., Crowley, M.A., et al.
items.why: A practical template for long, field-scale irrigation maps built from Landsat, machine learning and Google Earth Engine.

stages.title: Seeing irrigation in satellite soil moisture

items.title: Evaluating the utility of satellite soil moisture retrievals over irrigated areas and the ability of land data assimilation methods to correct for unmodeled processes
items.authors: Kumar, S.V., Peters-Lidard, C.D., Santanello, J.A., et al.
items.why: Explains why irrigation is hard for land models and data assimilation: it is a process most models leave out, yet it shows up in the observations.

items.title: Irrigation signals detected from SMAP soil moisture retrievals
items.authors: Lawston, P.M., Santanello, J.A., Kumar, S.V.
items.why: A short paper showing that SMAP soil moisture does carry an irrigation signal over US farmland.

items.title: How much water is used for irrigation? A new approach exploiting coarse resolution satellite soil moisture products
items.authors: Brocca, L., Tarpanelli, A., Filippucci, P., et al.
items.venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
items.why: Introduces the soil-moisture inversion idea (SM2RAIN) behind many later estimates of irrigation water use.

items.title: Estimating irrigation water use over the contiguous United States by combining satellite and reanalysis soil moisture data
items.authors: Zaussinger, F., Dorigo, W., Gruber, A., et al.
items.why: Scales the idea up: compares satellite soil moisture with a reanalysis that has no irrigation to estimate water use across the US.

items.title: Soil moisture data assimilation to estimate irrigation water use
items.authors: Abolafia-Rosenzweig, R., Livneh, B., Small, E. E., et al.
items.venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
items.why: The data assimilation route: synthetic experiments showing how assimilating soil moisture can recover irrigation amounts.

items.title: How accurately can we retrieve irrigation timing and water amounts from (satellite) soil moisture?
items.authors: Zappa, L., Schlaffer, S., Brocca, L., et al.
items.venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
items.why: Tests how resolution, revisit time and noise limit what satellite soil moisture can tell us about irrigation timing and amounts.

items.title: Long-term irrigation water use datasets from multiple Earth Observation-based methods in major irrigated regions
items.authors: Laluet, P., Dari, J., Busschaert, L., et al.
items.why: Long-term irrigation water use datasets from several satellite methods and a land surface model, ready to download and compare.
